literal: Flute is sweet, lute is sweet, they say, who their own children's lisping words have not heard.
translation: Only those who have not heard the lisping speech of their own children will say that the flute is sweet and the lute is sweet.
modern: தம்முடைய குழந்தைகளின் மழலைச் சொற்களைக் கேட்காதவர்களே, குழலின் ஓசையும் யாழின் ஓசையும் இனிமையானவை என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the incomparable sweetness of a child's early, imperfect speech, known as 'maḻalai'. The poet compares this natural sound to the flute and the lute, which were considered the pinnacle of sweet, refined music in classical times. To parents who have experienced the joy of hearing their own children babble, even these exquisite musical instruments sound secondary. Therefore, only those who are deprived of hearing their children's voices would praise instrumental music as the ultimate sweetness.
